cluster_name: French high school students nationwide protest underfunded schools
event_summary: French high school students held nationwide protests over teacher shortages and overcrowded classrooms, beginning in Paris suburbs around September 20 and spreading across France by early October 2026, resulting in over 2,000 arrests and more than 400 school closures.
tldr: The headline layer is dominated by the CRIME_PUNISHMENT register — nine outlets in seven countries reduce the story to arrests, riots, and clashes — while the structural cause (underfunded schools, teacher shortages) surfaces explicitly in only two headlines. US conservative outlets are the sharpest divergence: Daily Wire uses 'students riot' as a standalone predicate and Fox News embeds a government blame attribution ('points finger at hard left') directly into the headline, framings absent from every other outlet across 13 countries. The FAIRNESS framing — centering Paris's deprived suburbs as the story's origin — is confined to three headlines from Global South and wire-service outlets (Dawn, Reuters, Straits Times), meaning a reader seeing only Western headlines would have no indication that class inequality drives the movement. BBC's 'send shivers down the government's spine' is the most politically loaded headline from any public broadcaster, compressing the story into a political-crisis frame that erases the student-grievance dimension at first click.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only outlet to use 'riot' as the headline's active predicate for students ('As Students Riot'), stripping the protest of any political or grievance context — the most reductive characterisation of the movement in the corpus.

Only outlet to embed the French government's 'hard left' blame narrative directly into a headline, advertising the political scapegoating itself as the story rather than burying it as a body-text claim.

Only outlet to append '(VIDEOS)' parenthetically to the headline — a tabloid-spectacle marker absent from all other outlets — foregrounding shock visual content over the political or structural story.

Only outlet to lead with a student-voice quote in the headline ('We will not stop'), centering student agency and determination rather than government failure or police response — a frame entirely absent from the remaining 22 headlines.

bottom_line: At the headline layer, France's school protests are overwhelmingly sold as a law-enforcement story — arrests, riots, violence — while the structural inequality at its root (deprived Paris suburbs, underfunded schools, teacher shortages) is visible only in three headlines from Global South and wire-service outlets, confirming that the headline-body divergence is widest at Western outlets.
